2019_135_060419regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of June 4, 2019 at Athens High School. Twenty-five recognition items open the meeting, after which the consent agenda carries three sets of minutes, the April 2019 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements in period of $22,386,825.23, and three purchases — a Gorno Ford transport vehicle at $37,552.00, a Rochester Lawn Equipment tractor/loader at $30,969.12 and two ABB robotic arms at $50,519.00 for new Engineering Technologies courses. The single business item awards $205,895.11 of mechanical and electrical work for the Troy High auto and wood shop renovation, and the meeting closes in session on the Superintendent's evaluation.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, June 4, 2019, 7:00 PM, Athens High School. Agenda: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (items A through Y); Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General – Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Closed Session; Adjournment.

**Recognition**
Twenty-five items, read by Tim Fulcher and by board members in rotation. Item 2.A recognizes the Synchronized Swim State Champions and All-State Athletes under head coach Lori Uchwal with assistant coaches Erika Barker, Beth Borland and Katie Richardson. The rest are middle-school academic and arts results: a first-place national finish in the AMC8 (Boulan Park); Destination Imagination global-finals qualifiers from Boulan Park ("Lettuce Explode," Renaissance Award, "Game On" challenge) and Smith ("Super Peaches"); a FIRST Robotics state win (Baker and Boulan Park); Future Problem Solving state champions bound for the international conference in Massachusetts; MATHCOUNTS, Michigan Mathematics League, MIFA Forensics, Model United Nations, Purple Comet and three Quiz Bowl titles; the Schroeder Dragon Chess Team winning the Michigan State K-6 Chess Championship against a field of over 100 players; All-State Band and Orchestra selections; National French, German and Spanish exam awards; a National Geographic Bee state finalist; National History Bee qualifiers headed to Rosemont, Illinois on June 7th-9th; Scholastic Art and Writing awards; Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit winners invited to the Broadcom Masters; and Science Olympiad results, with Smith placing 3rd at the National Tournament.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the May 7, 2019 special meeting, the May 7, 2019 workshop and the May 21, 2019 meeting; the April 2019 Treasurer's Report; and three purchases. The May 7 special meeting selected D.M. Burr to perform the district's custodial, grounds and warehouse services following the Request for Proposals issued March 21, 2019, on a 6-0 vote with Hammond absent. The May 21 meeting ran to thirteen pages of minutes: a Wass Wolves' Wellness Night Mission Moment, the Coach-Athlete-Parent Pact from the Troy Athletic Advisory Committee, 25 Outstanding Support Staff nominees with Lori Uchwal named overall winner, 23 retirees, and Teacher Appreciation Week for May 6-10, 2019.

That meeting also made four administrative appointments effective July 1, 2019 — William Turner as Director of College & Career Programming, Kristin Martin and Michael Munaco as Assistant Principals at Athens High, and Christine DiPilato as Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction — adopted high school science materials for grades 9-12 at $631,107.36, authorized a Chartwells food service agreement for 2019/20 with four renewal options, and awarded playground safety surfacing to Rolar Property Services at $145,603.00, preschool technology at $117,601.85, flooring bid alternates to Conventional Carpet at $94,883.00, and Troy Preschool trim and door frames to Barton Malow at not more than $949,000.00 — the last on a 5-2 vote, Gottlieb and Hammond objecting that the scope had been missed in the original 2018 bid and the district should not bear the cost. Two resolutions passed 7-0: one commemorating the centennial of the 19th Amendment, noting Michigan was the second state to ratify and that the district will fly the Victory Flag June 10-14, 2019 and August 24-28, 2020; and one supporting Governor Gretchen Whitmer's budget recommendations and urging passage of the FY 2019-2020 state budget before July 1, 2019.

**Treasurer's Report — April 2019**
Check disbursements total $20,095,250.10 (General Fund $5,717,381.13, Special Revenue Funds $255,107.09, Other Funds $14,122,761.88), with ACH debits $50,328.82, outgoing wire transfers $2,062,940.53, P-Card purchases $178,888.78 and prior period voids ($583.00), giving total disbursements in period of $22,386,825.23. The Debt Funds line alone is 12,982,203.75, reflecting a $2,000,000.00 principal and $988,750.00 interest payment to Huntington National on the 2014 debt fund.

**Purchases and business**
Consent items award a transport vehicle to Gorno Ford at $37,552.00 and a tractor/loader to Rochester Lawn Equipment at $30,969.12, both off MiDEAL state contract pricing reviewed by Rob Carson, plus two robotic arms from ABB at $50,519.00 for the new Engineering Technologies courses at Athens and Troy High. Item 8.A awards Bid Package 30, the Troy High auto and wood shop mechanical and electrical upgrades under the 2013 Bond Program Series 2: CSM Mechanical at $80,645.11 and DeHondt Electrical at $108,250.00 with a 9% contingency of $17,000.00, totalling $205,895.11 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund.

**Closed session**
The Board resolves under Section 8(c) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act to enter closed session on the Superintendent's evaluation, with the Collins & Blaha evaluation tool attached: six components plus an optional seventh, rated highly effective through ineffective, with the overall rating weighted 75 percent evaluation tool and 25 percent student growth and assessment.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, June 4, 2019, 7:00 PM at Athens High School. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition (A through Y); 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Closed Session; 12. Adjournment.

**Recognition.** Item 2.A, read by Tim Fulcher, honors the Synchronized Swim State Champions and All-State Athletes; head coach Lori Uchwal is listed with assistant coaches Erika Barker, Beth Borland and Katie Richardson, followed by a long roster of swimmers. The remaining items are read by board members in rotation (Karl, Nancy, Gary, Paula, Steve, Elizabeth, Nicole). 2.B: a Boulan Park student placed 1st nationally in the American Mathematics Contest (AMC8). 2.C: Destination Imagination — Boulan Park's Troy Creative Minds "Lettuce Explode" team won first place at both regional and state tournaments and earned Destination Imagination's Renaissance Award for the "Game On" challenge in the Fine Arts category, while Smith's Super Peaches Team qualified for the global competition in Missouri in May after placing 1st at the state competition in East Lansing, raising travel money through gofundme.com and bake sales. 2.D: FIRST Robotics World Competition, Baker and Boulan Park — teams get six weeks to design, build, test and program a robot with a weight limit of 120 lbs., about 3 ft. x 3 ft. in size, followed by six weeks of district qualifying competitions, state championships and the world championship; the students won 1st in State. 2.E: Future Problem Solving (Global Issue), Larson and Smith — Larson placed 1st in State at the FPS State Bowl and students from both schools were invited to the International Conference in Massachusetts in June. 2.F: MATHCOUNTS, Boulan Park, 1st in State. 2.G: Michigan Mathematics League, Boulan Park, 1st in State in the individual division and as a team, plus Perfect Score and 1st Place 8th Grade Team in Michigan. 2.H: the Michigan State K-6 Chess Championship Tournament draws over 100 chess players from Michigan schools, and the Schroeder Dragon Chess Team finished first, winning the state championship. 2.I: MIFA Spring State Forensics, Boulan Park — 1st in State for Dramatic Interpretation, Impromptu, Informative, Oratory, Original Poetry and Sales. 2.J: Model United Nations/Red Cedar, Boulan Park — "Best Delegate in State." 2.K and 2.L: MSBOA All-State Middle School Band (Larson, 1st in State for flute and oboe) and Orchestra (Boulan Park, two students 1st in State), where an average of over 2,000 students audition each year for the 400 seats across five ensembles in 10-minute recorded auditions. 2.M: the Michigan All-State Middle School Honors Band and Orchestra drew over 1,000 auditioning students, with the top 100 chosen for band and 100 for orchestra, rehearsing three days in January in Grand Rapids at Michigan's Music Conference; four Smith students were accepted. 2.N: National French Contest/Le Grand Concours, Boulan Park and Larson, placed nationally. 2.O: National Geographic Bee, Smith — a seventh-grade student reached the Michigan Geographic Bee at Western Michigan University from a field of approximately three million students in almost 10,000 schools. 2.P: National German Exam, Baker and Larson, Gold and Silver awards. 2.Q: National History Bee, Smith — students competed at the Detroit Regional Finals in West Bloomfield in April and are National Final Qualifiers, competing at the National Level Bee June 7th-9th in Rosemont, IL, with starred students also qualifying for International Competition. 2.R: National Spanish Exam, Boulan Park, Silver and Bronze Awards. 2.S: Purple Comet Math Contest, Boulan Park — an international online team competition held every year since 2003 with teams of one to six students answering 15 problems; 1st in State. 2.T and 2.V: Quiz Bowl contests of 100 multiple-choice questions — Boulan Park took State Champions in the American Scholastic League event and 1st in State plus 1st and 6th in Nation in the other. 2.U: Quiz Bowl (NAQT), Smith — invited to Chicago, IL on May 10-12, 2018 after victories at Detroit Catholic High School and Detroit Country Day, finishing 1st Place at the Michigan All-State Middle School Quiz Bowl Championships. 2.W: Scholastic Art and Writing Awards, founded in 1923 for grades 7-12; Boulan Park students received Gold and Silver Key and Honorable Mention Awards. 2.X: Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit, held annually at Cobo Hall; Larson students won 1st in State for the Great Lakes Water Authority, Lemelson Foundation and SEFMD Grand Award and were invited to the Broadcom Masters National Science Fair. 2.Y: Science Olympiad — Baker placed 1st in State on heredity, and the Smith Knights placed 3rd at the National Tournament in April against over 1,000 middle school and high school students, ahead of all regional schools in Metro Detroit.

**Consent agenda.** Items A through G: minutes of the May 7, 2019 special meeting, the May 7, 2019 workshop and the May 21, 2019 meeting; the April 2019 Treasurer's Report; and the transport vehicle, tractor/loader and robotic arms purchases.

The May 7, 2019 special meeting minutes record President Schmidt calling the meeting to order at 5:35 p.m. at the Administration Building with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, Hammond absent, administrators Machesky, Griffor, Harris, Carrier and West in attendance and one member of the audience. Resolution 19-039, moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Fleming, recites the district's goal of 100% of stakeholders responding positively to the quality of their learning environment, the Request for Proposals for Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services issued March 21, 2019, and the Board's conclusion that it can maintain and enhance service levels by contracting with D.M. Burr; it selects D.M. Burr and authorizes the Superintendent or designee to negotiate and finalize terms subject to legal counsel review and to execute the contract with D.M. Burr Group. The vote was 6 yes, 0 no, Hammond absent; the certification cites the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. The meeting adjourned at 6:12 p.m.

The May 7 workshop began at 6:12 p.m. with the same members, Hammond absent, and administrators Fulcher, Soggs, Harris, West, Griffor, Carson and Jennifer Gottlieb plus approximately six others in the audience. The agenda covered a Teaching and Learning update (Athletics CAP Pact, review of achievement data, 1:1 high school pilot update), a Business Services update (food service bid, 2019 playground safety surfacing replacement, preschool technology, 2019-2020 budget development), and other items including a resolution in support of Governor Whitmer's budget proposal and a science materials review. It adjourned at 10:30 p.m.

The May 21, 2019 meeting at the Services Building began at 7:02 p.m. with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, Hammond participating by remote communication, administrators Fulcher, Jansen, Pagel, DiPonio, Dixon, Griffor, Whan, Turner, Jennifer Gottlieb, Harris and West, and approximately 200 members of the audience. The Mission Moment recognized Wass Elementary's Wass Wolves' Wellness Night, sponsored by the Wass PTO in January and aligned to the district's Red Pillar, "Attending to the Social-Emotional and Physical Well-Being of All"; physical education teacher Mark Cavataio introduced students Laura Witherspoon, Victor Pertile and Sahana Nair. Tim Fulcher, Director of Athletics and Enrichment, presented the Coach-Athlete-Parent (CAP) Pact finalized by the Troy Athletic Advisory Committee — four high school athletes, four parents, four coaches and the athletic directors — adapting a model originally created by Growing Great Relationships for implementation in the fall sports season; recognized were athletic directors Bob Dowd and Dan House, coaches Todd Heugh, Brian Miska, Stacie Klumpp and Chris Frasier, parents Colleen Lindgren, Greg Bright, Ross Parpart and Karen Christenson, and students Izzy Crum, Andrew Dionisio, Sawyer Darish and John Stabinsky. Twenty-five Outstanding Support Staff nominees were recognized with certificates and plants, among them Linda Alfonso, Bona Bita, Pam Byrd, Dean Cameron, Christine Clifford, Val Doozan, Karen Guilbert, Maxine Japowicz, Joaquina Kapuscinski, Sharon Kreza, Fran Mahoney, Jill Martens, Barb McCoy, Cathy Mishark, Nancy Mosey, Cindy Mounteer, Ashmi Parekh, Nancy Richter, Lynn Sharp, Melodi Stephens, Tara Stonecipher, Meena Trivedi, Melissa Verduyn and Melissa Vukov, with Lori Uchwal named Overall TSD Outstanding Support Staff. Twenty-three retirees were introduced, including Kent Hurst (Services Building, a dedicated employee since 1976), Glenn Rexer (Smith Middle, since 1977), Val Thudium (Costello, since 1977), Joan Levitt (Boulan Park, since 1980) and Debbie Rosenman (Barnard, since 1981). Resolution 19-040 supported National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 6-10, 2019, 7-0.

Consent resolution 19-041 approved the April 9, 2019 workshop minutes, the April 16, 2019 meeting minutes, the March 2019 Treasurer's Report, the Oakland Intermediate School District budget and a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2019/2020 budget. Four personnel resolutions each issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure: 19-042 William Turner as Director, College & Career Programming; 19-043 Kristin Martin as Assistant Principal, Athens High School; 19-044 Michael Munaco as Assistant Principal, Athens High School; and 19-045 Christine DiPilato as Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction — all effective July 1, 2019 and all 7-0. Student representatives reported: Jenna Doyle (Athens) on prom held May 11th and an 80's theme choir concert on the 16th; Erin McManus (Troy High) on the DECA class going to Orlando and over 2,000 students taking part in a 13-minute lip sync music video; Lauryn Collins (International Academy-East) on 370 seniors graduating May 30th at the Detroit Opera House and final exam week June 14-19; and Mackenzie Malinowski (Troy College & Career) on principal Deb MacDonald Linford retiring in June and TCCHS graduation on June 5th at Troy High School at 7:00 p.m. In public communication, Kirk Webber, a Troy resident on Carmel Drive, addressed the condition of the Athens baseball facilities and safety and upgrade concerns with a handout to all members; Jennifer Lee, a district teacher, addressed Performance Base Compensation and the attendance policy; and Ann Comiskey of the Troy Women's Association described the organization's programs and its Elf Shelf fundraiser.

Under curriculum, Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, reported on recommended high school science materials; Dr. Philippart asked whether the science equipment comes with text and Gottlieb noted online resources. Resolution 19-046 approved the science materials for grades 9-12 in the amount of $631,107.36 for the 2019-20 school year, 7-0. Business resolutions followed: 19-047 authorized administration to finalize an agreement with Chartwells for food services for 2019/20 with options to renew for 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24, contingent on final approval by the Michigan Department of Education and consistent with the Request For Proposal dated March 18, 2019; 19-048 awarded playground loose fill surfacing material to Rolar Property Services, Inc. at $145,603.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund; 19-049 awarded preschool technology at $117,601.85 from the Early Childhood Center Fund, with Mrs. Soggs confirming the cost includes installation, wiring and cabling; 19-050 awarded flooring replacement bid alternates to Conventional Carpet at $94,883.00 from the Building Site and Sinking Fund; and 19-051 awarded Troy Preschool trim and door frames to Barton Malow in an amount not to exceed $949,000.00 from the Early Childhood Capital Projects Fund. Mr. West explained that the trim and door frame scope had been missed in the original bid in 2018 and stressed a 4-6-week material lead time plus another 4-6 weeks for labor against an August preschool opening; Mr. Gottlieb said he would vote against it and did not think staff was responsible for the error, and Mrs. Hammond said the district should not be incurring the cost and recommended Barton Malow provide other solutions. It carried 5 yes, 2 no (Gottlieb, Hammond).

Two resolutions closed the May meeting. 19-052 commemorates the 100th anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment, reciting that Michigan women cast their vote on June 10, 1919 when Michigan ratified — the second state to do so — that the amendment was ratified August 26, 1920, and that August 26, 2020 marks the centennial; the district will fly the 19th Amendment Victory Flag June 10, 2019 through June 14, 2019 and August 24, 2020 through August 28, 2020. 19-053 supports proper funding of education in Michigan, citing the non-partisan School Finance Research Collaborative, endorsing Governor Gretchen Whitmer's budget recommendations and urging the Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 state budget prior to July 1, 2019. Both passed 7-0. In board comments Mr. Schmidt bid farewell to Jennifer Gottlieb, who had been offered a position with Oakland Schools, calling her the epicenter of deep learning; Mrs. Fleming noted the TFEE Golf Outing at Sanctuary Lake on June 21st with 8:00 a.m. registration, a 9:30 shotgun start and dinner at 3:30; and Dr. Machesky listed the Buddy Bench Ribbon Cutting with Troy Rotary and the Mayor, a Suicide Prevention Community Discussion forum, IA graduation May 30th, Athens and Troy High graduations at the O'Rena on Saturday June 1st and TCCHS on June 5th. The meeting adjourned at 9:17 p.m.

**Closed session: Superintendent evaluation.** Item 11.A asks the Board to resolve, as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to go into closed session to discuss the Superintendent's evaluation, with a roll call vote of Wilson, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Schmidt and no further business afterward except adjournment. The attached Superintendent Evaluation System, prepared by Collins & Blaha, P.C., notes that the Michigan Revised School Code requires boards to evaluate superintendents annually and evaluates performance across six components — Visionary Leadership, Policy and Governance, Instructional Leadership, Communication and Community Relations, Organizational Management, and Professionalism and Ethics — with an optional seventh component for statutory factors including proficiency with the teacher evaluation tool under section 1249, progress on school improvement plans, pupil attendance, stakeholder feedback and goal achievement. Board members rate each component highly effective, effective, minimally effective or ineffective and submit individual forms to the Board President; those forms are not retained and are exempt from disclosure under MCL 15.243(1)(m), though the Board's final evaluation is subject to FOIA, and the decision to adopt an overall rating must be made in open session under MCL 15.263. Under MCL 380.1249b(1)(b), 25% of the annual evaluation must be based on student growth and assessment data, the aggregate data used in teacher year-end evaluations district-wide. Ratings convert to numerical scores of 4, 3, 2 and 1; the overall rating is 75% of the performance evaluation tool rating and 25% of the student growth and assessment rating, computed by multiplying the tool score by 7.5 and the assessment score by 2.5, with sums of 40-35 highly effective, 34-25 effective, 24-15 minimally effective and 14-10 ineffective.
